newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backed dip, spreads little changed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backed dip, spreads little changed.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities dipped lower, performing on par with to slightly better than their Treasury counterparts on Tuesday, market experts said.
Mortgages were flat to 3/32 lower overall, while comparable Treasuries fell 2/32 to 4/32.
Light buying in 8.0s and 8.5s bolstered pass-through prices early in the day, but the market began to sell off across the board by midday, traders said.
"We were having a stellar day until the buying gave up around noon," said the head trader of a New York-based firm.
"At one point, we were about eight or nine basis points tighter (to Treasuries) over the last two days," he said, adding that his firm had been buying 8.0s and 8.5s.
However, profit-taking prevailed as pass-throughs were held in negative territory.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 2/32 at 99-24/32, yielding 102 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was down 2/32 as well, at 99-22/32 and 99-27/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 4/32 at 99-19/32, yielding 6.56 percent.
Looking forward, traders were questioning whether or not pass-throughs could sustain their performance to Treasuries.
"The big question is how far they are going to go to Treasuries," said one regional trader.
Technically, the current resistance levels will be tough to break unless the market gets big news, he said, adding that might come with Friday's payrolls data.
"For now, it's sit and wait," he said.
